name: Puke
lede: Puke is an old English name for a dark, woolen-cloth color, not the olive yellow its modern swatch suggests.

sections.title: A dark wool
sections.body:
Paterson gives puke as a blackish color once used in relation to wool [1]. St Clair, in her glossary of color names, calls it dark brown and says it was named after a woolen fabric [2]. Books disagree on whether it was black or brown, though both place it at the dark end and both tie it to cloth [1][2]. Paterson lists it among the blacks in its index [1].

Neither book says when the word began or where the fabric came from, so its origin is undocumented here [1][2].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The library value is a vivid olive yellow, nothing like the dark color the two books describe [3]. The modern slang sense of the word explains the swatch, not the history, and no book here discusses it [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Seven paintings of 23,781 in our archive carry a close match covering at least 5% of the canvas [4]. The strongest is a Basohli folio of about 1760, at roughly 60% of the page [4].

origin.named_after: a woolen fabric (St Clair); origin otherwise undocumented
